content:
Hi everyone,

I am sharing a project where the proof was produced by GPT-5.5 Pro and the Lean formalization by Codex.

The result concerns the Kannan–Tetali–Vempala (KTV) conjecture for the binary fixed-margin swap chain. For an m × n binary matrix with fixed row and column sums, the chain repeatedly picks two rows and two columns and performs the usual rectangle swap when possible; KTV asks for polynomial-time mixing of this chain.

The formalized theorem is the explicit spectral-gap bound for the 1/2-lazy chain:
gap >= 1 / (choose m 2 * choose n 2)
corresponding to Theorem 2.2 of our paper "Spectral Gap for the Binary Fixed-Margin Swap Chain". This spectral-gap bound implies the conjectured polynomial-time mixing.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22636
Main repo: https://github.com/guanyangwang/ktv-swap-lean
Audit repo: https://github.com/guanyangwang/ktv-swap-lean-comparator

The audit repo follows the Challenge/Solution pattern: ChallengeDefs.lean imports only Mathlib and defines the statement surface, Challenge.lean states the theorem, and Solution.lean imports the proof library and proves the same statement. It also includes formalization.yaml, comparator.json, and a GitHub Actions workflow running the comparator.

The main repo builds locally, #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, and the comparator workflow passes on GitHub Actions. The main repository took roughly 100 hours to produce, using about one week of GPT Pro quota.

Feedback would be very welcome!
